title: First Identification of 10 kpc [C II] 158 μm Halos around Star-forming Galaxies at z = 5-7
question: Do normal star-forming galaxies at z=5-7 have extended (~10 kpc) [CII] 158um halos, and how do they compare with the dust and stellar continuum, Lya halos and simulations?

data.sensitivity: Stacked continuum rms 4.1 (ALMA-ALL) and 8.3 (ALMA-HST) uJy/beam; per-source 8-64 uJy/beam

what.value: Leclercq et al. Lya halo scale lengths from MUSE (6 LAEs at z>5)

evidence.quote: we use the recent results with the deep MUSE data for the high-$z$ LAEs of (cite: leclercq2017)
global scale $L_{\rm [CII]}$/SFR$_{\rm total}$ ratios of the local dwarf galaxies (cite: delooze2014)
we show the $L_{\rm [CII]}$/SFR$_{\rm total}$ ratios of the extended emission around local LIRGs

recipe.method: CASA standard calibration, tclean cubes at 20 km/s and continuum, uv continuum subtraction for 4 sources
Velocity-integrated map, peak position on uv-tapered (0.6'') map, Gaussian fit to 1.2'' aperture spectrum for peak and FWHM, then re-integrate over 2xFWHM
Extract +-50 km/s line channels (and line-removed continuum), shift centers with stacker, concat, statwt reweight
8''x8'' stamps, remove low-z contaminants with galfit Sersic, noise-weighted average, convolve to ALMA beam with 3-Sersic galfit kernel
Radial surface brightness of dirty images; SFR_IR and SFR_UV from Murphy+11 with modified blackbody
assumptions: beta=1.8, Td=35 K, single Gaussian line FWHM 270 km/s to correct 100 km/s window

recipe.method: Two-component Sersic (central, fixed from HST) + exponential halo with galfit; uvmultifit visibility fits as check
Stack simulated [CII], FIR, UV images (9 of 48 Althaea; 12 Halo images) and smooth to ALMA beam

evidence.quote: 21$\sigma$ (20$\sigma$) and 10$\sigma$ (8$\sigma$) significance levels for the line and dust continuum
We obtain the best-fit scale-length values of $r_{\rm n}=$ 3.3 $\pm$ 0.1 kpc.
best-fit effective radius of $r_{\rm e}=5.6$ $\pm$ 0.1 kpc
The median $r_{\rm n}$ value for the 6 LAEs is estimated to be $3.8\pm1.7$ kpc

answer_key.quantity: Stacked spectrum core and broad FWHM

evidence.quote: 296 $\pm$ 40 km/s and 799 $\pm$ 654 km/s for the core and broad components
The highest ratios ($> 10^{8}\, L_{\odot}\,M_{\odot}^{-1}\,{\rm yr}$) are found at the outer regions

not_stated_but_needed: Exact flux re-calibrations and extra flagging per dataset
Random-aperture method details and radial bin definitions
Aperture/continuum image parameters beyond natural weighting
missing_for_reproduction: Radial bin definitions and noise estimation details
score_reason: Public data and clear stacking recipe, but many parameters unstated and simulations unavailable.
rediscovery_reason: Data are archival, the stacking recipe is mostly described, and results are numeric (scale length, S/N).
